findings: The archive README defines a and c dimensions and rim width as two-camera-view averages; minimum errors come from the view difference and maximum errors add per-camera measurement error.
The two member headers label -50 C, 970 or 972 hPa, 48 percent supersaturation, and a 48-to-20 percent forcing step at 230 minutes, but do not define the supersaturation reference or its uncertainty.
The bounded S5 check confirmed DOI 10.1175/JAS-D-25-0030.1 as the first report; publisher access is paywalled, OpenAlex exposes no open full text, and no public manuscript was located.
Related Penn State papers use ice-supersaturation notation, but lineage convention is not a substitute for the missing first-report method definition.

findings: The 2013 analysis assumed pressure-independent prism attachment kinetics and used that premise when concluding that terrace-width-dependent basal attachment kinetics were required to explain column growth near -5 C.
The 2016 paper explicitly negates that pressure-invariance premise and the resulting basal-terrace conclusion near -5 C.
The correction does not retract the raw 2013 height and radius observations and does not negate the separately stated near--15 C prism-terrace hypothesis.
